results.title: Asiedu Nketiah urges African parties to look beyond elections, build institutions for 2040
results.content: National Democratic Congress (NDC) Chairman Johnson Asiedu Nketiah has called on African political parties to strengthen their institutional capacity and prepare leaders capable of addressing the continent’s long-term development challenges. He said political parties must look beyond winning elections and invest in the knowledge, expertise and structures needed to govern effectively. Mr Asiedu Nketiah made the call in an acceptance address after assuming office as inaugural Chair of the African Political Parties Initiative (APPI) at the African Political Parties Summit 2026 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on Saturday, November 7.

results.title: ECG to begin nationwide revenue mobilisation exercise, warns customers with arrears of disconnection
results.content: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) will begin a nationwide Mass Revenue Mobilisation Exercise on Monday, November 9, to recover outstanding electricity bills from customers. The exercise will run until Friday, November 27, 2026, and will cover all categories of customers with arrears, including residential, commercial and industrial customers, as well as Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs).

results.title: Traffitech rollout: What Ghana can learn from countries that warn motorists about speed cameras
results.content: The rollout of Ghana’s automated traffic enforcement system, Traffitech, has brought into sharp focus an important aspect of road safety management: the responsibility of authorities to provide motorists with adequate road signs before enforcing traffic regulations. As concerns grow over inadequate speed-limit signs and the absence of advance warnings about enforcement cameras, experiences from developed jurisdictions suggest that Ghana could benefit from a more comprehensive approach that combines technology, clear road signage, public education and effective enforcement.

results.title: Tokenising government securities could attract more foreign investors to Ghana – WeWire CEO
results.content: The Chief Executive Officer of WeWire, Ebenezer Ghanney, says tokenising Ghana's government securities could make it easier for international investors to access the domestic market and expand the government's sources of funding. He believes issuing digital tokens linked to government bonds and Treasury instruments could reduce some of the traditional barriers that make it difficult for foreign investors to participate in Ghana's financial market. Speaking at the Africa Virtual Assets Summit (AVSA) in Accra, Mr Ghanney identified government securities as among the financial products that could be relatively easy to tokenise because existing market structures and custody arrangements are already in place. “Government securities are easier because the product doesn't require heavy lifting like gold. With gold, we need to make sure that we have the custody sorted out,” he said.
